summary:
A Charter newsletter issue combining AI-and-work news briefs with an interview excerpt from the Charter Workplace Summit (Oct. 21) featuring Theresita Richard, Patagonia's chief people and culture officer and global head of justice and belonging, in conversation with Charter co-founder Erin Grau.

News briefs: A US Senate bill led by Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the Stability and Opportunity for Workers Act, would provide up to two years of income support for workers displaced by AI, expand unemployment insurance, and pilot tuition assistance for job training; it is one of two AI bills signaling Democratic priorities before the midterms. An Apollo Global Management report found AI has delivered no financial payoff outside the tech sector, based on revenue per worker, profit margins, and productivity growth across S&P 500 firms, arguing AI cannot grasp accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs, or fairness. A Goldman Sachs analysis (via Fortune) found AI-displaced workers take roughly a month longer to find full-time work. Anthropic's IPO filing listed loss of worker trust as a risk factor, citing possible decline in morale, disillusionment, loss of trust in leadership, or reduced productivity.

Patagonia interview: Richard describes a philosophy of treating people "like humans" and "like adults," grounded in authenticity, entrepreneurship, agency, ownership, and mutual accountability. Rising costs forced a two-year pause on tuition reimbursement, handled through open trade-off conversations with employees; a reimagined offering is returning. She frames Patagonia life as "swimming in a sea of contradictions" (quoting first CEO Kris Tompkins), citing the "don't buy this jacket" ad, and says it would be irresponsible for Patagonia to stay out of the AI conversation despite AI's uneven community impacts and "shadow side." On civic engagement, Patagonia offers paid time off to vote and activism hours on a nonpartisan basis, and covers bail for full- and part-time employees arrested during peaceful protest.
